segments.text: The round robin is in the rear view and we've got everything you need to know about the semi-finals at the WTA Finals Riyadh presented by PIF in the Flash 5 for Day 7.
Number one. Well, Courtney, we have come to expect the unexpected from Barbara Krejcikova,
and she delivered once again. Dropped her opening match here in Riyadh, proceeds to
win the Orange Group. She's booked a semifinal matchup against Zhang Xinwen at six o'clock
Friday night. It's a quick turnaround. What do you think we can expect? I mean,
I don't even know what to expect of Barbara Karchikova anymore because when she is good,
she is one of the absolute best and she showed that so far.
Hasn't beaten Jung Shun-wen, is 0-1 against her. They last played in Jeong Jo last year,
but any given day, Barbara Karchikova can play as the best player in the world.
And so that's a big test for Jung Shun-wen.
I love that I asked if I could ask you what to expect after I just said,
we have no idea what to expect. You're exactly right.
I am right there with you.
In our second semi-final, we've got the world number one,
Irina Sabalenka, taking on Coco Gauff, who will have to rebound
after her loss to Barbara Krejcikova on Thursday.
What are you thinking here?
Tough one. Four and four, very dead even, head to head
between Coco and Irina, but Irina Sabalenka, as is befitting
of the world number one 2-0 against Coco this year.
It'll be a rematch of the U.S. Open final, which is the last time that Coco
did get a win over Sabalenka, very tough on a quicker court you have to like
Sabalenka but she'll have to rebound from her loss in the last match of the
group stages against Elena Rabokina. Number three it is time to talk some
doubles we've got Dabrowski and Rautlef facing Perez and Melikar
Martinez and in our other semi-final it's Siniakova and
Townsend facing Chan and Kudramedova. A lot going on with these two
matchups what sticks out to you? Yeah I mean for me I really love the
that the Final Four is bringing to the table, you've got kind of pure double
specialists with Routlef and Dabrowski, as well as Melikar Martinez and Perez,
and you've got two teams that are, you know, a good mix of that singles and
doubles vibe with Townsend and Siniakova, as well as Gudermettova and
Chan. So, you know, it's nice to see that in, you know, the showcase of
doubles, you have both styles of teams succeeding here in Riyadh. And two
undefeated teams, as well. We've got Siniakova and Townsend, and Routlef and
Dabrowski, both 3-0 so far.
Yeah, very difficult to do here.
For number 4, Blair, you wanted to shout out the fan zone.
I sure did.
I've been out there every day.
We've had some incredible Q&As with former players.
Our tournament director, Garbine Muguruza.
We've had Lucy Safarova out there.
We had the first female professional Saudi tennis
player in Yara Al-Hagbani.
It was an incredible experience for the fans
to be able to interact with professional athletes,
sometimes for the very first time.
And again, just even me getting a chance to talk to them.
Their eyes light up, they've had so much fun,
and it seems meaningful in a way that it might not be in some other places in the world.
So it's been a really special experience.
Shout-out to our amazing Fanzone organizers here at the WTA Finals.
And number five, we've got some more quotable quotes from the press room.
Courtney, what was your favorite?
Yeah, for me, I'm going to go with Igor Šviantek.
I think that it was a tricky situation for her to come into Riyadh
with a little bit, you know, not enough match play maybe, but she kind of had a nice reflection
on her season, a season that she should be very proud of.
Overall, I think this season was pretty great and a lot of, you know, different
challenges that I handled well.
I won many tournaments again.
I was able to play consistently and even develop, you know, and stay number one
for so long that it's, you know, beyond my expectations and everything I ever thought
about, you know, myself.
So I'm really proud of myself.
For me, it was Jung-Chin Wen giving a very candid answer,
as we've come to expect, about who calls
the shots in her practices.
I remember at the beginning, we
fight a lot about that because sometimes I
like to do the things I feel is working on me.
And then sometimes he thinks, no, you should do this
because you need to improve that.
We had a lot of disgust for that moment.
But after when I started to grow and play better
and better with better ranking,
And then he said, okay, during the tournament, especially before the matches, when you are in the warmup, you do what you want.
You manage your own practice, but when the training season comes, you have to listen to the coach because, you know, as a player, you can't dominate the practice all the time.
That's all for your Flash Five. On day seven, go to wtatennis.com for all of the latest from the WTA Finals.
Riad presented by PIF, and we'll see you tomorrow.
